Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:10:1.hebrew: אם כן מצינו לר"י תם משלם יותר מחצי נזק - א"כ, דלא דריש ר"י "פחת שפחתתו מיתה מחצין בחי", מצינו בתם משלם יותר מחצי נזק. והיכי דמי? שור שוה נ' שנגח לשור שוה מ', והנבילה יפה כ', והוי נזק כ', ופלגא נזקא עשרה. וכי פלגי חצי חי וחצי מת, נוטל ניזק בחי כ"ה ובמת י', הרי [ל"ה]; נמצא מזיק משלם יותר מחצי נזק. דבשלמא לר"מ לא משלם אלא חצי מה שפחתתו מיתה, אלא לר"י — נהי נמי דהיכא דמטי חצי החי יותר מנזק שלם, נפקא ליה האי דלא שקיל ניזק חצי החי מקל וחומר ממועד, כדקתני לעיל: "מה מועד חמור אינו משלם אלא מה שהזיק, תם הקל לא כ"ש?" — אבל הכא דליכא למימר הכי, דהא פחות ממה שהזיק משלם, ומיהו טפי מחצי נזק איכא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:10:1.english: If so, we find according to Rabbi Yehuda [that] an innocuous [ox] pays more than half the damage - If so, since Rabbi Yehuda does not expound [that] they divide the depreciation caused by the death out of the live [ox], we find in [the case of] an innocuous [ox that] it pays more than half the damage. And how is this case? An ox worth fifty [zuz] that gored an ox worth forty, and the carcass is worth twenty; thus the damage is twenty, and half the damage is ten. And when they divide half the live [ox] and half the dead [ox], the injured party takes twenty-five from the live [ox] and ten from the dead [ox], which is [thirty-five] — thus the damager ends up paying more than half the damage. For granted, according to Rabbi Meir, he only pays half of what the death depreciated [it]; but according to Rabbi Yehuda — even though where half of the live [ox] amounts to more than full damage, he derives this [law] that the injured party does not take half of the live [ox] from an a fortiori inference from a forewarned [ox], as was taught above: "Just as a stringent forewarned [ox] only pays what it damaged, should not a lenient innocuous [ox] all the more so [not pay more than what it damaged]?" — nevertheless here, where one cannot say this, since behold he pays less than what he damaged, yet there is more than half the damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:11:1.hebrew: אית ליה לרבי יהודה פחת שפחתתו מיתה - הלכך, בההוא נמי מקרא נפקא ליה דלא שקיל אלא חצי נזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:11:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] the depreciation that death caused - Therefore, in that [case] too, he derives from a verse that he takes only half-damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:13:1.hebrew: א"כ - דלפחת שפחתתו מיתה לחוד אתא, לכתוב "את המת יחצון"; מאי "וגם"? ש"מ תרתי, דשתפיה רחמנא בשבחא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:13:1.english: If so - [that the verse] comes only for the depreciation that death caused it, let [it] write, "the dead [ox] they shall divide." What is [the purpose of] "and also"? Learn from it two [things]: that the Merciful One made him a partner in the appreciation [of the carcass].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:15:1.english: [If] his ox humiliated [a person], he is exempt - As we have established (above, Bava Kamma 26a): "[When] a man [inflicts a blemish] upon his fellow," and not an ox upon his fellow.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:16:1.english: [If] his ox set fire to a haystack on Shabbat, he is liable - [He pays] half-damages, because it is unusual.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:17:1.english: All who act destructively are exempt - With regard to Shabbat.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:17:2.hebrew: חוץ מחובל ומבעיר - כדמפרש טעמא במס' שבת בפרק האורג: מדאצטריך קרא למישרי מילה, מכלל דשאר חובל חייב; ומדאסר רחמנא שריפת בת כהן בשבת, דמקלקל הוא, מכלל דמקלקל בהבערה חייב, כגון השורף כלי, דמקלקל הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:17:2.english: Except for one who injures or kindles [a fire] - As the reason is explained in Tractate Shabbat in the chapter [entitled] HaOreg: Since a verse was needed to permit circumcision [on Shabbat], it follows by implication that any other case of injuring is liable; and since the Merciful One prohibited the burning of a priest's daughter on Shabbat — which is a destructive act — it follows by implication that one who acts destructively through kindling is liable, such as one who burns a vessel, which is a destructive act.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:17:3.english: [It] is not a mishna - For they too are exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:17:4.hebrew: בצריך לכלבו - דהוי מקלקל על מנת לתקן. והא (דתנן) נצרר הדם, אע"פ שלא יצא, משום צובע הוא דמחייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:17:4.english: Where he requires [the blood] for his dog - For it is [a case of] acting destructively in order to repair. And [as for] that which we learned [in a Mishnah], "[If] the blood congealed [under the skin], even though it did not come out, [he is liable]" — it is on account of dyeing that he is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:1:1.hebrew: תם חמור ממועד - דהא גבי מועד אמרינן בפ"ק (דף י:) בעלים מטפלים בנבילה, דכתיב "והמת יהיה לו" וגו' — לניזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:1:1.english: An innocuous [ox] is more stringent than a forewarned [ox] - For regarding a forewarned [ox], we say in the first chapter (10b) [that] the owner deals with the carcass, as it is written: "and the dead [animal] shall be his," etc. — [i.e., belonging] to the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:2:1.hebrew: הכי נמי - דס"ל תם חמור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:2:1.english: Indeed [so] - that he holds an innocuous [ox] is more stringent.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:2:2.english: As we learned - Later, in the chapter [entitled] Shor Shenagach Arba'ah VaChamishah [An Ox That Gored Four or Five].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:2:3.hebrew: ר"י אומר תם חייב - אם שמרו שמירה פחותה ויצא והזיק, ומועד פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:2:3.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: An innocuous [ox] is liable - If he guarded it with an inferior guarding and it went out and caused damage, and a forewarned [ox] is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:2:4.english: As verses are written - As [the Gemara] explains there.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:3:1.hebrew: זה נוטל חצי החי - ששוה חציו י"ב סלעין ופלגא בשביל תשלומין שלו, שלא שוה אלא ה' סלעים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:3:1.english: This [one] takes half of the living [ox] - Whose half is worth twelve and a half selaim for his payment, [even] though [his ox] was only worth five selaim.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:4:1.hebrew: תם הקל לא כ"ש - אלמא לר' יהודה, תם קל קרי ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:4:1.english: An innocuous [ox], the lenient [one], [is it] not all the more so - Thus, according to Rabbi Yehuda, he calls an innocuous [ox] "lenient."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:5:1.hebrew: ר"מ סבר שבח נבילה דניזק הוי - דלית להו שום שותפות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:5:1.english: Rabbi Meir holds [that] the appreciation of the carcass belongs to the injured party - For they have no partnership [in it].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:6:1.hebrew: והיינו דקשיא ליה לר"י - דשמעינן ליה בברייתא דלקמן דקאמר: "יכול שור שוה ה' סלעים שנגח לשור שוה מנה כו'". דהא דקאמר "יכול", משום דקשיא ליה הכי: כיון דלדידיה ס"ל דחס רחמנא עליה דמזיק למשקל בשבחא, יכול שור שוה חמש סלעים שנגח לשור שוה מנה והנבילה יפה נ' זוזים, דשקיל מזיק חצי החי דהוו שני סלעים ופלגא, וחצי המת דהוו שש סלעים ורביע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:6:1.english: And this is what was difficult for Rabbi Yehuda - For we hear him [saying] in the baraita below, where he says: "Could [it be that] an ox worth five sela gored an ox worth a maneh, etc.?" For that which he says "could [it be]" is because this was difficult for him: since according to him he holds that the Merciful One had mercy on the damager to take [a share] of the increased value, could [it be that if] an ox worth five sela gored an ox worth a maneh, and the carcass is worth fifty zuz, that the damager takes half of the live [ox], which is two and a half sela, and half of the dead [ox], which is six and a quarter sela?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:7:1.hebrew: אמרת וכי היכן מצינו מזיק נשכר - שאינו מפסיד כלום, דאע"ג דקאמר ר"י לעיל דמזיק שקיל בשבחא, בתשלומי ח"נ מיהא איתא ומפסיד ע"ה משור החי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:7:1.english: You say: And where do we find a damager who profits - That he does not lose anything; for even though Rabbi Yehuda said above that the damager takes [a share] of the appreciation [of the carcass], he is nevertheless [liable] for the payment of half-damages, and he loses [a portion] from the live ox.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:7:2.hebrew: שלם ישלם - במועד כתיב; אלא שני תשלומים כתב לך — אחד לתם ואחד למועד — לומר: בעלים משלמין ואין הבעלים נוטלין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:7:2.english: He shall surely pay - [This] is written regarding a mu'ad [forewarned ox]; rather, [Scripture] wrote two payments for you — one for a tam [innocuous ox] and one for a mu'ad — to say [that] the owners pay, and the owners do not take.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:8:1.hebrew: והנבילה יפה שלשים זוז - שהוקרה הנבילה משמתה, דשקיל מזיק חמשה זוזי באותן י' זוזי שהשביחה, דהא לא מטי פסידא לניזק, דהוא נמי מרויח ה' דינר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34b:8:1.english: And the carcass is worth thirty zuz - [Meaning] that the carcass appreciated in value after it died, so that the damager takes five zuz of those ten zuz by which it appreciated, for no loss comes to the injured party, as he also profits five dinars.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:10:1.hebrew: והתורה אמרה ומכרו - לאו משום דלשתמע פשטיה דקרא ח"נ, דקרא לא משמע כלל. אלא י"ל דה"ק: "והתורה אמרה ומכרו", וע"כ ר"י לא מפרש לקרא דלשתלם כל שעה יותר מחצי, דהא שמעינן ליה לר"י דאית ליה ח"נ לקמן בפ' שור שנגח ד' וה' (בבא קמא ד' לז.) — אמר להן: "לשבתות משלם נזק שלם, ולימי החול משלם חצי נזק":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:10:1.english: But the Torah stated: "Then they shall sell..." - [This is] not because the plain meaning of the verse implies half-damage, for the verse does not imply [that] at all. Rather, one can say that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: "But the Torah stated: 'Then they shall sell [the live ox]...'" — and perforce Rabbi Yehuda does not interpret the verse [to mean] that he should always pay more than half [the damage], for we have heard regarding Rabbi Yehuda that he holds [the law of] half-damage below in the chapter [entitled] Shor SheNagach Arba'ah VaChamishah (Bava Kamma 37a), [where] he said to them: "For Sabbaths he pays full damage, and for weekdays he pays half-damage."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:15:1.hebrew: שורו שבייש פטור - צער ורפוי ושבת ודמי ולדות לא חשיב, משום דשמעינן ממתניתין דהחובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף פז.). ואע"ג דבושת נמי קתני התם, מ"מ תנא הכא לדקדק "הוא" דומיא ד"שורו", או "שורו" דומיא דידיה. וכן "שור שהדליק הגדיש" אצטריך להכי כדאיתא בגמרא, דלמילתא אחריתי לא אצטריך דפשיטא דחייב, דלענין שורו מה לי שבת ומה לי חול? ואגב "הדליק הגדיש" דמיירי בנדון בנפשו, קתני "חבל באביו ואמו". אבל "שורו שסימא את עין עבדו" אצטריך, שאע"פ שבעצמו חייב — בשורו פטור, דהא לא אשמועינן בשום משנה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:15:1.english: If his ox humiliated [someone], he is exempt - [The Mishnah] does not list pain, healing, loss of livelihood, and the value of unborn children, because we learn [them] from the Mishnah in [the chapter] HaChovel (later, Bava Kamma 87a). And even though humiliation is also taught there, nevertheless [the Tanna] taught [it] here to infer "he" analogous to "his ox," or "his ox" analogous to "him." And similarly, "an ox that set fire to a stack of grain" was needed for this [purpose], as is stated in the Gemara; for regarding any other matter it would not be needed, since it is obvious that he is liable — for with respect to his ox, what difference is there between Shabbat and a weekday? And incidentally to "set fire to a stack of grain," which deals with one who is judged with a capital offense, [the Mishnah] teaches "one who wounded his father or mother." However, "his ox that blinded the eye of his slave" was needed [on its own], because even though when he himself [does it] he is liable, when his ox [does it] he is exempt — for [the Tanna] did not teach us this in any [other] Mishnah.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:17:1.hebrew: חובל וצריך לכלבו מבעיר וצריך לאפרו - רבינו שמואל פירש דר' אבהו סבר כר"ש דאמר מקלקל בחבורה חייב, ורבי יוחנן ס"ל כר' יהודה דאמר מקלקל בחבורה ובהבערה פטור, וצריך לכלבו או לאפרו לא חשיב מקלקל אלא מתקן, דחייב אפי' לר"י. וקשה, דא"כ אמאי א"ל "פוק תני לברא"? אטו משום דס"ל כר"י, מאן דמתני כרבי שמעון משתיקין ליה?! דכה"ג פריך בפ"ק דחולין (דף טו.). ע"כ נראה דר' אבהו ורבי יוחנן אליבא דר"ש פליגי: דרבי אבהו כר"ש כדאיתא פרק האורג (שבת דף קו. ושם ד"ה חוץ), ורבי יוחנן סבר דאפי' רבי שמעון בעי תקון קצת, ומיהו לא חשיב תקון שיתחייב בכך לרבי יהודה או לר"ש בשאר מלאכות, דאין דרך לחבול בחבירו ליתן לכלבו ולשרוף גדיש בעבור אפר; וטעמא בחובל ומבעיר כדמפרש התם בפרק האורג, משום דגמר ממילה והבערת בת כהן. וא"ת: ואמאי מחייב רבי אבהו אע"פ שאין צריך לכלבו ולאפרו? הא כיון דאין צריך כלל, מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה היא, דאע"ג דמחייב ר"ש מקלקל בחבורה, מ"מ בעינן צריכה לגופה, כדמוכח בריש הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פד: ושם ד"ה מאן) ובשלהי כל כתבי (שבת דף קכא.) ובפרק כלל גדול (שבת דף עה. ושם ד"ה טפי) ובשלהי ספק אכל (כריתות דף כ:)! ואור"י דכל הנך סוגיות כרבי יוחנן, וההיא דספק אכל ופרק כל כתבי דהוי ברייתא, איכא למימר דההוא תנא סבר כר"י בחדא וכרבי שמעון בחדא. ועי"ל דאפי' במקלקל גמור משכחת לה דהיא צריכה לגופה, כגון חובל באיסורי הנאה שסבור שיכול ליהנות ליתן לכלבו, וכן מבעיר באיסורי הנאה שסובר שיכול לבשל בו קדירה. וא"ת: ורבי יוחנן, מאי טעמא דלא מחייב מקלקל גמור? דהא טעמא דמקלקלין פטורין היינו משום דבעינן מלאכת מחשבת, כדמוכח בספ"ק דחגיגה (דף י:), ולענין חבורה לא חיישינן אמלאכת מחשבת, כדמוכח בס"פ ספק אכל (כריתות דף יט:) דאמר "הנח לחבורה, הואיל ומקלקל חייב מתעסק נמי מחייב", ומתעסק לא מפטר אלא מטעם מלאכת מחשבת! וי"ל: נהי דלא בעינן מלאכת מחשבת, מיהו כיון דגמרינן ממילה ומהבערת בת כהן, לא מחייבינן אלא דומיא דהנהו, דלא הוי מקלקל גמור אלא תקון במקצת; ור' אבהו — נהי דצורך מצוה לא משוי ליה תקון, מ"מ צריכה לגופה משוי ליה מה שהוא צריך למצוה. וא"ת: צריך לכלבו ולאפרו היכי חשיב צריכה לגופה? מ"ש מחופר גומא ואין צריך אלא לאפרה? וי"ל דלא דמי: דהכא צריך הוא לנטילת נשמה, דהיינו הדם — "כי הדם הוא הנפש" — כדי לתת לכלבו, ומבעיר נמי להבערה כדי לעשות אפר, כמו מבעיר לבשל קדירה; ולא דמי לחופר גומא, דממילא ואין נהנה כלל ממנו. וא"ת: הא דאמר בפ"ק דיבמות (דף ו:) דאצטריך קרא למיסר הבערת בת כהן משום דהוה ס"ד למשרי מקל וחומר דעבודה דדחיא שבת — תיפוק ליה דאי לא כתיב הבערת בת כהן הוה שרינן כל המקלקלין בהבערה! וי"ל דהתם כר' יהודה, דחשיב ליה תקון:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:17:1.english: One who injures and needs [the blood] for his dog; one who kindles and needs its ashes - Rabbeinu Shmuel explained that Rabbi Abbahu holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says that one who acts destructively by inflicting a wound is liable, whereas Rabbi Yoḥanan holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says that one who acts destructively by inflicting a wound or by kindling is exempt, and [a case where] he needs [the blood] for his dog or [needs it] for its ashes is not considered acting destructively, but rather acting constructively, for which one is liable even according to Rabbi Yehuda. And this is difficult: for if so, why did he say to him, "Go out and teach it outside"? Is it possible that because he [Rabbi Yoḥanan] holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, anyone who teaches a baraita in accordance with Rabbi Shimon is silenced?! For [the Gemara] raises a similar objection in the first chapter of Chullin (15a). Therefore, it appears that Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagree according to Rabbi Shimon: for Rabbi Abbahu [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, as is stated in chapter HaOreg (Shabbat 106a, and ibid., s.v. ḥutz), whereas Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that even Rabbi Shimon requires a slight constructive element, though it is not considered [enough of] a constructive act for one to be liable thereby according to Rabbi Yehuda, or according to Rabbi Shimon with respect to other labors — for it is not the normal manner to injure one's fellow in order to give [the blood] to one's dog, or to burn a stack of grain for the sake of ashes; and the reason [one is liable] for injuring and kindling is as explained there in chapter HaOreg, because it is derived from circumcision and the burning of a priest's daughter. And if you ask: Why does Rabbi Abbahu hold one liable even when he does not need [the blood] for his dog or [need it] for its ashes? Since he does not need it at all, it is a labor not needed for its own sake (melakhah she'einah tzerikhah legufah); for even though Rabbi Shimon holds one who acts destructively by inflicting a wound liable, nevertheless we require that it be needed for its own sake, as is proven at the beginning of HaNeḥnakin (Sanhedrin 84b, and ibid., s.v. man), and at the end of Kol Kitvei (Shabbat 121a), and in chapter Kelal Gadol (Shabbat 75a, and ibid., s.v. tefei), and at the end of Safek Akhal (Keritot 20b)! And Rabbeinu Yitzḥak says that all those sugyot follow Rabbi Yoḥanan, and [as for] that [passage] in Safek Akhal and chapter Kol Kitvei, which is a baraita, one can say that that Tanna holds like Rabbi Yehuda in one [matter] and like Rabbi Shimon in one [matter]. And one can also say that even in a case of purely destructive action, you can find [a case] where it is needed for its own sake — for example, one who injures [an animal] forbidden for benefit, thinking that he is permitted to benefit [from it] to give [its blood] to his dog; and likewise, one who kindles [wood] forbidden for benefit, thinking that he can cook a pot with it. And if you ask: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, what is the reason that one is not liable for a purely destructive act? For the reason that those who act destructively are exempt is because we require purposeful craftsmanship (melekhet maḥashevet), as is proven at the end of the first chapter of Chagigah (10b), whereas regarding inflicting a wound we are not concerned about purposeful craftsmanship, as is proven at the end of chapter Safek Akhal (Keritot 19b), where it says, "Leave aside inflicting a wound, for since one who acts destructively is liable, one who acts preoccupiedly (mit'asek) is also liable" — and one who acts preoccupiedly is only exempt on account of [the requirement of] purposeful craftsmanship! And one can answer: Although we do not require purposeful craftsmanship, nevertheless, since we derive [liability] from circumcision and from the burning of a priest's daughter, we only hold [a person] liable in cases similar to those, which are not purely destructive but rather constructive to a slight degree. And [as for] Rabbi Abbahu — although the need of a mitzvah does not render it constructive, nevertheless the fact that it is needed for the mitzvah renders it [a labor] needed for its own sake. And if you ask: How is "needing [the blood] for his dog or [needing it] for its ashes" considered [a labor] needed for its own sake? How is it different from one who digs a pit and only needs its dirt? And one can answer that it is not comparable: for here he needs the taking of life, which is the blood — [as the verse states,] "for the blood is the life" — in order to give to his dog; and one who kindles also [needs] the kindling in order to produce ashes, just like one who kindles to cook a pot. And it is not comparable to one who digs a pit, for [the pit comes about] incidentally and he does not benefit from it at all. And if you ask: [Regarding] what is said in the first chapter of Yevamot (6b), that a verse was needed to prohibit the burning of a priest's daughter [on Shabbat] because one might have thought to permit it by an a fortiori argument (kal vaḥomer) from the Temple service, which overrides Shabbat — let it be derived [instead that the verse is needed] because if the burning of a priest's daughter were not written, we would have permitted all destructive acts of kindling! And one can answer that there [it is] according to Rabbi Yehuda, who considers it constructive.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:1:1.hebrew: מצינו תם חמור ממועד - וא"ת: והא ר"י אית ליה (לקמן בבא קמא דף מה:) צד תמות במקומה עומדת? וי"ל: דה"פ: מצינו צד תמות חמור מצד מועד, ומייתי מברייתא דשור שוה מנה כו' — ומה צד מועד דחמור אין משלם אלא מה שהזיק, צד תמות הקל לא כל שכן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34b:1:1.english: We have found [that] an innocuous [ox] is more stringent than a forewarned [ox] - And if you will say: Does Rabbi Yehuda not hold (below, Bava Kamma 45b) [that] the innocuous aspect remains in its place? And one can answer: This is what it means: We have found [that] the innocuous aspect is more stringent than the forewarned aspect, and [the Gemara] brings [proof] from the baraita of "an ox worth a maneh," etc. — for if the forewarned aspect, which is stringent, pays only what it damaged, [should] the innocuous aspect, which is lenient, not all the more so?
